content.thinking:
Under the RRA, the tenant needs to give two months' notice, and that period doesn't need to align with the rent period end date. With notice served by email on 10 October, the earliest possible end date would be 10 December 2026, assuming deemed service applies from that date.

An earlier departure would only be possible if the landlord agrees in writing, via surrender agreement or a replacement tenant being found—so this needs to go to the landlord for approval rather than being decided unilaterally. I'll reply to the tenant explaining the one-month notice isn't valid, confirm the two-month requirement and 10 December earliest date, note they can ask the landlord about flexibility, and clarify that rent continues until then and the deposit will be returned per the scheme timeline after tenancy ends—without inventing details like a keys drop-off address. This isn't a maintenance issue so no ticket is needed; I'll send the tenant message, request landlord approval, and schedule a follow-up.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month's notice isn't enough to end the tenancy on 10 November. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays payable up to the day the tenancy ends.

If you need to leave sooner, your landlord can agree to an earlier end date, but only in writing. I'm asking them now and will tell you their answer. I can't promise they'll agree. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you've heard from us in writing.

Keys: please hold on to them for now. We'll confirm the handover details and a check-out appointment once the end date is settled.

Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. Once the tenancy has ended and keys are back, we'll check the property against the check-in record and deal with the deposit through the scheme. I can't give an exact date yet, as it depends on the end date and the check-out.

You'll hear from us again by Wednesday 14 October.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

options: Hold to the legal date: tenancy ends 10 Dec 2026 (recommended unless you want an early re-let)
Agree in writing to end on 10 Nov 2026 (surrender by agreement)
Agree to another date between 10 Nov and 10 Dec
Start marketing the flat now for a re-let from 10 Dec

content.thinking:
Under the RRA, the tenant needs to give two months' notice, and that period doesn't need to align with the rent period end date. With notice served by email on 10 October, the earliest possible end date would be 10 December 2026, assuming deemed service applies from that date.

An earlier departure would only be possible if the landlord agrees in writing, via surrender agreement or a replacement tenant being found—so this needs to go to the landlord for approval rather than being decided unilaterally. I'll reply to the tenant explaining the one-month notice isn't valid, confirm the two-month requirement and 10 December earliest date, note they can ask the landlord about flexibility, and clarify that rent continues until then and the deposit will be returned per the scheme timeline after tenancy ends—without inventing details like a keys drop-off address. This isn't a maintenance issue so no ticket is needed; I'll send the tenant message, request landlord approval, and schedule a follow-up.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month's notice isn't enough to end the tenancy on 10 November. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays payable up to the day the tenancy ends.

If you need to leave sooner, your landlord can agree to an earlier end date, but only in writing. I'm asking them now and will tell you their answer. I can't promise they'll agree. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you've heard from us in writing.

Keys: please hold on to them for now. We'll confirm the handover details and a check-out appointment once the end date is settled.

Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. Once the tenancy has ended and keys are back, we'll check the property against the check-in record and deal with the deposit through the scheme. I can't give an exact date yet, as it depends on the end date and the check-out.

You'll hear from us again by Wednesday 14 October.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
